column1: # Chained forward application of Function-typed params — the compose family
# (design/legacy/checker-compiler-completeness-review.0.ignore §2.1, found 2026-08-02 as
# a live miscompile: the whole-frame replay's flat window lost the source's
# paren structure, so `f (g x)` compiled the RET count error where the
# interpreter applies both fns; noteDynFrameReplay then declined the >1-
# applicable window soundly). GRADUATED 2026-08-03 in three coordinated
# steps — see checker-compiler-completeness-review.0.md §9.6b/§9.8:
#   1. the Stage-G single-arg increment: a leading one-arg fn-carrier apply
#      `(g x)` records the trailing spelling's RecordDynApply event, so
#      compose / twice / depth-3 chains / mid-body applies compile natively
#      (rows in lang/spec/fn-value.tsv §8);
#   2. checkModeParenFnCollapse (the plain-surface collapse twin) killed
#      the def-split checker FALSE POSITIVE — `def r (f x)` no longer flags
#      undefined_word on the def-bound name
#      (lang/go/check_fn_param_apply_def_fp_test.go, now the positive pin);
#   3. the replayIsBodyTail windowReadsID widening (a dyn-bind of a value
#      the window READS is not a reorderable event) armed the def-split
#      body tail, so the stage spelling compiles natively too.
# Remaining edge (no ledger entry needed — the rows compile or decline in
# the §9.1 "unapplied fn-value" class pinned in
# lang/go/bytecode_chained_apply_test.go): a CHAINED MULTI-ARG apply
# `f (g x y)` keeps declining — beyond one argument the leading and trailing
# spellings' collection orders diverge, so the inner group never collapses.
# The row below is the unledgered CONTROL: it must keep compiling natively.
def sel1 fn [[f:Function g:Function x:Integer] [Integer] [f x]] sel1 ([a:Integer] => [a mul 2]) ([b:Integer] => [b add 3]) 4
column3: control: two Function params, ONE applicable in the window — keeps compiling natively
